programmes.name: EUDP – Energiteknologisk Udviklings- og Demonstrationsprogram
programmes.summary: Denmark's main grant programme for development and demonstration of new energy technologies (TRL 4–8). Two rounds per year (I: spring, II: autumn). Typical projects are consortia of companies and universities/GTS institutes; international partners are allowed when the project advances Danish energy technology.
programmes.summaryDa: Danmarks største tilskudsprogram til udvikling og demonstration af ny energiteknologi (TRL 4–8). To runder om året. Typisk konsortier af virksomheder og videninstitutioner; udenlandske partnere tilladt, hvis projektet fremmer dansk energiteknologi.
programmes.maxFundingNote: No formal cap; typical grants DKK 3–30m. 2026-II pool DKK 240m + DKK 61.3m pyrolysis pool.
programmes.fundingRate: GBER rates: experimental development 25–45% (+15 pp collaboration bonus), industrial research 50–70%, demonstration up to 45–60%; universities/GTS up to 90%.

deadlines.note: Pattern: call published ~December, deadline late February. Verify on eudp.dk.

programmes.name: Innobooster
programmes.summary: Investment of DKK 200,000–5,000,000 (max 35% of project costs) in development projects of Danish SMEs (<250 employees). Requires either DKK 100k risk capital/grants raised in the last 3 years or gross profit ≥ DKK 250k in one of the last 3 annual accounts. Several application pools per year; max 24 months.
programmes.maxFundingNote: DKK 200k–1m under de minimis; DKK 1–5m under GBER.

deadlines.note: Listed by fondsradar.dk as next deadline – confirm on danmarksinnovationsfond.dk.

programmes.name: Innofounder
programmes.summary: Grant + mentoring for early-stage founders (recent graduates / pre-seed teams) building a knowledge-based startup in Denmark. Monthly grant for the founder(s) plus a small development budget for up to 12 months. Two rounds per year.
programmes.maxFundingNote: Approx.: monthly founder grant + development budget; check current guidelines.

deadlines.note: Spring round usually closes in February/March.

programmes.name: Innoexplorer
programmes.summary: DKK 0.5–1.5m for employees at Danish public research institutions, universities and hospitals to mature commercially promising research results before founding a company. 2026 themes: green tech, life science, critical & digital tech (plus non-themed pool).

programmes.name: Grand Solutions
programmes.summary: Large strategic R&D projects (typically DKK 5–30m investment) in consortia of companies and research institutions within thematic calls (green, life science, critical & digital tech, quantum, biosolutions, defence). Two-phase process: expression of interest (phase 1) and full application (phase 2).
programmes.maxFundingNote: Typical DKK 5–30m; larger in some calls.
programmes.fundingRate: Companies per GBER (typ. 25–70%), research institutions up to 90%; total public share usually ≤ 75%.

deadlines.note: Call usually opens in e-grant early January; verify themes in December.

programmes.name: MUDP – Miljøteknologisk Udviklings- og Demonstrationsprogram
programmes.summary: Grants for environmental technology: pre-projects and ETV verification (SMEs, de minimis), development/test/demonstration projects (GBER) and full-scale flagship (fyrtårn) projects. ≈ DKK 130m per year; one annual call published in February with staggered deadlines.
programmes.maxFundingNote: Pre-projects typically < DKK 0.5m; development/demo DKK 1–10m; flagship up to ≈ DKK 20m.
programmes.fundingRate: SME pre-projects/ETV up to 100% under de minimis (capped); development 25–60% per GBER; flagship demo up to 45–60%.

deadlines.note: 2026 call was published 6 Feb; deadlines April–August.

programmes.name: EIFO – Danmarks Eksport- og Investeringsfond
programmes.summary: Denmark's state export and investment fund: loans, guarantees, export credits and equity (direct venture investments and fund-of-funds) for Danish companies at all stages, including green transition loans. Rolling applications – no deadlines; bank co-financing is common.
programmes.maxFundingNote: Loans from ≈ DKK 1m; venture tickets typically DKK 5–100m.
programmes.fundingRate: Debt/equity on market-conform terms (not a grant).

programmes.name: Industriens Fond
programmes.summary: Private foundation funding projects that strengthen the competitiveness of Danish industry (themes: digitalisation, green transition, entrepreneurship, competences). Open applications year-round plus thematic calls.
programmes.fundingRate: Grant; typically for non-profit/knowledge-sharing projects with broad industry benefit.

programmes.name: Nopef – Nordic Project Fund
programmes.summary: Up to EUR 50,000 (max 50% of costs) for feasibility studies by Nordic SMEs on internationalising green solutions to markets outside the EU/EFTA. Conditional loan: fully converted to a grant if the project leads to an international establishment, 50% otherwise. Six deadlines per year; 5–6 weeks processing.
programmes.fundingRate: Max 50% of approved feasibility study costs.

programmes.name: Nordic Innovation – calls for proposals
programmes.summary: Thematic calls (green & competitive Nordic region, circular economy, critical raw materials, talent, mobility). Projects require partners from at least three Nordic countries and typically 50% co-funding. Grants up to ≈ NOK 2–6m depending on call.
programmes.maxFundingNote: Call-specific; e.g. talent call up to NOK 2m.

deadlines.call: Secondary critical raw materials value chains

programmes.name: EIC Accelerator
programmes.summary: Grant up to EUR 2.5m (TRL 6→8, max 24 months) and/or equity EUR 1–10m (up to EUR 30m via STEP) for single startups/SMEs with breakthrough, market-creating innovations. Short application any time (batched monthly, first Tuesday 17:00 Brussels); full application at six cut-offs per year; jury interview. Seal of Excellence for scores ≥ 13/15.
programmes.maxFundingNote: Grant ≤ EUR 2.5m; equity EUR 1–10m (STEP Scale-Up EUR 10–30m).
programmes.fundingRate: Grant 70% of eligible costs (100% for non-profit); equity at market terms.

deadlines.note: WP2027 not yet published; 2026 pattern = 6 bimonthly cut-offs.

programmes.name: EIC Pathfinder (Open & Challenges)
programmes.summary: 100% grants for visionary early-stage research (TRL 1–4): Pathfinder Open up to EUR 3m for consortia of ≥ 3 entities from 3 countries; Pathfinder Challenges up to EUR 4m (single applicants allowed) in defined topics. 2026 budget EUR 262m.

programmes.name: EIC Transition
programmes.summary: Up to EUR 2.5m (100%) to mature results from EIC Pathfinder, ERC Proof of Concept and selected Horizon projects from TRL 3 to TRL 5–6 and develop a business case. Single applicants (SMEs, spin-offs, research orgs) or consortia of 2–5 entities. One deadline per year; 2026 budget EUR 100m.

programmes.name: EIC STEP Scale-Up
programmes.summary: Equity-only investments of EUR 10–30m in startups, SMEs and small mid-caps (≤ 499 employees) scaling strategic technologies (digital & deep tech, clean tech, biotech). Continuous submission evaluated in batches; 2026 budget EUR 300m.

programmes.name: Eurostars (Eureka)
programmes.agency: Eureka Secretariat + national funding bodies (DK: Innovationsfonden; PL: NCBR)
programmes.summary: Transnational market-oriented R&D projects led by an innovative SME: ≥ 2 independent entities from ≥ 2 Eurostars countries (≥ 1 EU/AC), ≤ 36 months, SMEs ≥ 50% of costs, no participant/country > 70%. Funding paid nationally (Denmark: max EUR 300k per participant / EUR 500k if several Danish partners; Poland via NCBR). Two calls per year (March & September).
programmes.maxFundingNote: DK: EUR 300k/participant (EUR 500k for several DK participants). PL (NCBR): up to ≈ PLN 1.5–2m per project; rates depend on country.
programmes.fundingRate: Country-specific: DK SMEs ≈ 60% (dev.) / large ≈ 40%; PL SMEs up to 60–80%.

deadlines.note: Pattern: opens mid-January, closes mid/late March.

programmes.name: Horizon Europe – Cluster 5 (Climate, Energy & Mobility)
programmes.summary: Collaborative R&I projects (RIA 100%, IA 70% for companies) in energy supply, energy use, mobility and climate science. Consortia of ≥ 3 entities from 3 different MS/AC; typical grants EUR 3–15m. 2026 topics closed Feb–April 2026; 2027 topics expected to open autumn 2026.

programmes.name: EU Innovation Fund (Net-Zero Technologies)
programmes.summary: One of the largest funds for first-of-a-kind commercial demonstration of net-zero technologies (TRL 8+): general decarbonisation projects (small EUR 2.5–20m capex, medium 20–100m, large > 100m), clean-tech manufacturing and pilots. Grant up to 60% of relevant costs. Annual call; IF25 closed April 2026, IF26 expected to open Q4 2026 with deadline ≈ April 2027.
programmes.maxFundingNote: No cap; awards from a few EUR m to > EUR 200m.
programmes.fundingRate: Up to 60% of relevant costs (capex + opex delta).

programmes.name: LIFE Programme – Standard Action Projects
programmes.summary: EU programme for environment and climate action: circular economy & quality of life, nature & biodiversity, climate mitigation/adaptation/governance, clean energy transition. Standard Action Projects EUR 1–5m, 60% co-funding (up to 75% for priority habitats). Single beneficiary allowed; consortia common.

programmes.name: Digital Europe Programme
programmes.summary: Deployment-oriented funding for AI, data, cloud, cybersecurity, advanced digital skills and digital public services (50% co-funding SME/large, 100% for some coordination actions). Consortia usually ≥ 3 entities from 3 countries. 10th call round: opened 21 April 2026, deadline 1 October 2026.

programmes.name: CEF Energy – Cross-Border Renewable Energy (CB RES)
programmes.summary: Two-step scheme: first obtain CB RES status (6th status call open 29 Jun – 6 Oct 2026, budget EUR 150m for later works), then apply for grants for studies and works (final works call expected 2027). Projects must involve ≥ 2 Member States (or MS + third country) in renewable generation/cross-border cooperation.
programmes.maxFundingNote: Studies up to 50%, works typically up to 50%.

programmes.name: Interreg South Baltic – small-scale projects
programmes.summary: Cross-border cooperation between Poland, Denmark, Germany, Lithuania and Sweden (South Baltic coastal regions). Small-scale projects ≈ EUR 50–200k ERDF, 80% co-funding, partners from ≥ 2 programme countries. 4th small-scale call: 16 Sep – 4 Nov 2026.
programmes.maxFundingNote: Small-scale ≈ EUR 50–200k; regular projects up to ≈ EUR 2m.
